events.title: In the Room: Sixty Years on the Front Lines of History
events.description: Roosevelt understood the camera before most politicians did. He posed in buckskin in the Badlands, stood with John Muir at Yosemite, and left behind one of the most photographed lives of his century. David Hume Kennerly has spent sixty years doing the other half of that job — from the Vietnam battlefields that earned him the Pulitzer, to the Ford White House, to nearly every administration since. The special exhibition, drawn from his book In the Room, opens at the Library in October.

events.title: Books & Banter: "The Cloak" by Nickolai Gogol
events.description:
“Books and Banter,” a monthly book club featuring Victorian-era literature, will meet Tuesday, Nov. 17, 9-10 a.m. at the Chateau de Morès Interpretive Center in Medora. Book selections are intended to be easy to read and fun to discuss. Coffee and tea will be provided.

This month’s book, “The Cloak” by Nickolai Gogol was originally written in Russian, one of the seven languages Medora von Hoffman spoke! The book tells the story of a quiet clerk whose life changes after he buys a new coat. The book is available to read for free via Project Gutenberg.

When the State Historical Society of North Dakota took possession of the Chateau de Morès, it held a library so extensive that locals would borrow its books. The subjects of these books range from poems to military tactics, early childhood education to romance novels, and animal husbandry to human medical care.

This event is part of the ND250 commemoration celebrating our country’s 250th birthday.

For more information, contact Outreach Coordinator Shelby Reidle, shschateau@nd.gov or 701.623.4355. The Chateau de Morès State Historic Site is managed by the State Historical Society of North Dakota. The Chateau de Morès Interpretive Center hours are Tuesday-Saturday, 9 a.m.-5 p.m., and closed Sunday-Monday. The home is open by appointment. All times listed are Mountain time. Find information about upcoming programs of the State Historical Society at history.nd.gov/events.

events.title: Books & Banter: "A Christmas Carol" by Charles Dickens
events.description:
“Books and Banter,” a monthly book club featuring Victorian-era literature, will meet Tuesday, Dec. 15, 9-10 a.m. MT at the Chateau de Morès Interpretive Center in Medora. Book selections are intended to be easy to read and fun to discuss. Coffee and tea will be provided.

This month’s book, “A Christmas Carol” by Charles Dickens, tells the story of Ebenezer Scrooge, a bitter man who changes his ways after visits from three ghosts. Through their lessons, he learns kindness, generosity, and the true meaning of Christmas. This Victorian novella helped establish Christmas traditions in Great Britain and beyond. The book is available to read for free via Project Gutenberg.

When the State Historical Society of North Dakota took possession of the Chateau de Morès, it held a library so extensive that locals would borrow its books. The subjects of these books range from poems to military tactics, early childhood education to romance novels, and animal husbandry to human medical care.

This event is part of the ND250 commemoration celebrating our country’s 250th birthday.

For more information, contact Outreach Coordinator Shelby Reidle, shschateau@nd.gov or 701.623.4355. The Chateau de Morès State Historic Site is managed by the State Historical Society of North Dakota. The Chateau de Morès Interpretive Center hours are Tuesday-Saturday, 9 a.m.-5 p.m., and closed Sunday-Monday. The home is open by appointment. All times listed are Mountain time. Find information about upcoming programs of the State Historical Society at history.nd.gov/events.

Tickets do not include a stay at the Menger Hotel.

events.title: Girlfriend Getaway 2027
events.description:
About the Girlfriend Getaway

The Girlfriend Getaway was created from a simple belief: women need spaces where they can reconnect with themselves and with each other.

So many of us spend our days caring for everyone else. Managing it all. Showing up for everyone around us. Somewhere along the way, it gets easy to lose touch with ourselves.

This is now our fourth year gathering, and every time, the same thing happens. Women who don’t know a single soul in the room leave feeling like they’ve found their people.

Three days at the Rough Rider Hotel in Medora, ND. Speakers who share real stories, not polished performances. Small group conversations. Time built in just for you: a massage, a facial, reiki, whatever kind of care your body and heart are asking for. And plenty of open space too, to wander Medora, find a coffee shop, read a book, breathe.

You don’t have to come with a plan. You don’t have to come with friends. You just have to come as you are.

If this is your first time, welcome. You’re exactly where you’re meant to be. If you are returning, we can’t wait to see you again.

Ready to grab your spot? Tickets and all the details are linked above. And be sure to tap Going or Interested so you don’t miss updates as we get closer, we’ll be sharing more in the Discussion tab along the way.

events.title: 11th European Heart Congress
events.description:
The 11th European Heart Congress, taking place on August 09–10, 2027, in London, UK, is a premier international platform dedicated to advancing heart health, cardiac research, innovative therapies, advanced diagnostics, interventional procedures, and patient-centered cardiac care. The congress will bring together cardiologists, heart specialists, interventional specialists, cardiac surgeons, electrophysiologists, heart researchers, physicians, healthcare professionals, academicians, pharmaceutical and biotechnology experts, medical device specialists, and healthcare technology innovators to exchange knowledge, research, clinical experiences, and emerging developments in heart medicine and cardiac care.

Under the theme “Heart Health in a New Era: Innovation, Precision Medicine & Advanced Cardiac Care,” the congress will explore the rapidly evolving landscape of heart health and cardiac medicine, focusing on precision medicine, advanced heart diagnostics, innovative treatments, minimally invasive procedures, digital heart health, artificial intelligence, heart disease prevention, and personalized approaches to cardiac care. The scientific program will address major areas including coronary artery disease, heart attacks, acute coronary syndromes, heart failure, hypertension, cardiomyopathies, heart valve disease, arrhythmias, electrophysiology, structural heart disease, cardiac imaging, preventive heart care, congenital heart disease, and emerging cardiac therapies.
